text: Eric Cross's The Tailor and Ansty was banned by the Irish censor soon after its publication in 1942, because of its alleged earthy content. A Seanad debate opposing the prohibition ran for four days, and the sections quoted in the Senate were struck from the official record. Three priests forced Timothy Buckley to burn his own copy of the book. In 1963 the Censorship Appeals Board reviewed it and decided it was not obscene, and a new edition followed.
